topic: European Trading Companies & Struggle for Supremacy

items.front: Order of European arrival in India?
items.back: Portuguese (1498) → Dutch → English → Danish → French. But companies founded: English 1600, Dutch VOC 1602, French 1664.
items.examPoint: Sequence of European arrival (Portuguese → Dutch → English → Danish → French)
items.source: notes

items.front: Who reached Calicut in 1498 and who received him?
items.back: Vasco da Gama; received by the Zamorin of Calicut. First fort at Cochin (1503).
items.examPoint: Vasco da Gama (1498, Calicut, Zamorin) & the Cape route
items.source: notes

items.front: Who captured Goa (1510) and from whom?
items.back: Alfonso de Albuquerque, from the Sultan of Bijapur; real founder of Portuguese power in the East.
items.examPoint: Almeida's Blue Water Policy & Albuquerque's capture of Goa (1510)
items.source: notes

items.front: Dutch first factory & Coromandel HQ?
items.back: First factory Masulipatnam (1605); Fort Geldria at Pulicat = Dutch Coromandel HQ. Beaten by English at Bedara (1759).
items.examPoint: Dutch East India Company — first factory at Masulipatnam (1605) & decline
items.source: notes

items.front: English EIC — charter and first factory?
items.back: Chartered by Elizabeth I (31 Dec 1600); first factory Surat (1613) after Battle of Swally (1612).
items.examPoint: English EIC Charter of 1600 & early factories (Surat, Madras, Bombay)
items.source: notes

items.front: How did the English acquire Madras and Bombay?
items.back: Madras = Fort St George (1639); Bombay = Catherine of Braganza's dowry (1661), to EIC 1668.
items.examPoint: English EIC Charter of 1600 & early factories (Surat, Madras, Bombay)
items.source: notes

items.front: Danish company — dates?
items.back: Company 1616; factory Tranquebar (1620); sold to British 1845. Known for missionary work.
items.examPoint: Danish East India Company — Tranquebar (1620), sold to British (1845)
items.source: notes

items.front: French — Pondicherry founder & key figure?
items.back: Company reorganised by Colbert (1664); Francois Martin founded Pondicherry (1674); Dupleix began political intervention.
items.examPoint: French East India Company — Pondicherry (1674) & Dupleix
items.source: notes

items.front: Decisive battle sealing British supremacy over French?
items.back: Battle of Wandiwash (1760): Eyre Coote beat Count de Lally. Third Carnatic War ended by Treaty of Paris (1763).
items.examPoint: Third Carnatic War — Battle of Wandiwash (1760) & Treaty of Paris (1763)
items.source: notes

items.front: Carnatic War treaties in order?
items.back: 1st → Aix-la-Chapelle (1748); 2nd → Pondicherry (Dupleix recalled); 3rd → Paris (1763).
items.examPoint: First Carnatic War (1746–48) & Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle
items.source: notes

items.front: Plassey vs Buxar — who fought whom?
items.back: Plassey (1757): Clive v. Siraj-ud-Daulah (Mir Jafar's betrayal). Buxar (1764): Munro v. Mir Qasim + Shuja-ud-Daulah + Shah Alam II.
items.examPoint: Battle of Plassey (1757), Battle of Buxar (1764) & Diwani / Treaty of Allahabad (1765)
items.source: notes

items.front: What did the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) grant?
items.back: Diwani (revenue rights) of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the Company — trader turned territorial ruler.
items.examPoint: Battle of Plassey (1757), Battle of Buxar (1764) & Diwani / Treaty of Allahabad (1765)
items.source: notes

items.front: Northern Circars — 5 tracts?
items.back: Srikakulam (Chicacole), Rajahmundry, Eluru, Kondapalli, Guntur. Bussy got them from Nizam; farman 1765; Guntur to British 1788.
items.examPoint: Northern Circars — French acquisition & transfer to the British
items.source: notes

items.front: Charter Acts — end of EIC trade?
items.back: 1813 ends monopoly except tea/China; 1833 ends all trade + creates GG of India; 1853 opens Civil Service. Company rule ends 1858.
items.examPoint: Charter Acts of the EIC (1813 monopoly ends except tea/China; 1833 all trade ends & GG of India; 1853) & end of Company rule (GoI Act 1858, Queen's Proclamation)
items.source: notes

items.front: Bengal staple exports (mid-18th c.)?
items.back: Cotton textiles, raw silk, saltpetre and opium.
items.examPoint: Bengal staple exports (cotton, silk, saltpetre, opium) & St Francis Xavier (Jesuit, Bom Jesus Basilica Goa)
items.source: notes

items.front: Yanam — which power, and merger?
items.back: French enclave near the Godavari mouth; merged de facto with India in 1954, now part of Puducherry UT.
items.examPoint: AP-coast factories — Bheemunipatnam & Yanam (French, merged 1954)
items.source: notes
